# A comment after the colon of a multi-line conditional is kept.
celfmt -i plain.cel
! stderr .
cmp stdout want_plain.txt

celfmt -i want_plain.txt
! stderr .
cmp stdout want_plain.txt

# The else branch is not cuddled onto the colon when there is a comment.
celfmt -i nested.cel
! stderr .
cmp stdout want_nested.txt

celfmt -i want_nested.txt
! stderr .
cmp stdout want_nested.txt

# The comment may follow the colon without a space, and a colon in a string
# on the first line of the else branch is not mistaken for it.
celfmt -i tight.cel
! stderr .
cmp stdout want_tight.txt

celfmt -i string.cel
! stderr .
cmp stdout want_string.txt

# Text in the else branch is not a comment, even when it has a colon followed
# by two slashes, on the line after the colon or further into the branch.
celfmt -i url.cel
! stderr .
cmp stdout url.cel

celfmt -i deep.cel
! stderr .
cmp stdout deep.cel

# The comment is kept when the true branch spans several lines.
celfmt -i multi.cel
! stderr .
cmp stdout want_multi.txt

celfmt -i want_multi.txt
! stderr .
cmp stdout want_multi.txt

-- plain.cel --
state.a ?
	state.b
: // c1
	state.d
-- want_plain.txt --
state.a ?
	state.b
: // c1
	state.d
-- nested.cel --
state.a ?
	state.b
: // c2
	(
		state.d ? state.e : state.f
	)
-- want_nested.txt --
state.a ?
	state.b
: // c2
	state.d ? state.e : state.f
-- tight.cel --
state.a ?
	state.b
:// c3
	state.d
-- want_tight.txt --
state.a ?
	state.b
: // c3
	state.d
-- string.cel --
state.a ?
	state.b
: "http://example.com"
-- want_string.txt --
state.a ?
	state.b
:
	"http://example.com"
-- url.cel --
state.a ?
	state.b
:
	"https://example.com"
-- deep.cel --
state.a ?
	state.b
:
	state.links.map(attr,
		attr.matches("^<https?://")
	).filter(x,
		x
	)
-- multi.cel --
state.a ?
	{
		"a": 1,
		"b": 2,
	}
: // c4
	state.d ?
		state.e
	:
		state.f
-- want_multi.txt --
state.a ?
	{
		"a": 1,
		"b": 2,
	}
: // c4
	state.d ?
		state.e
	:
		state.f
